reviewedPosts.author: jerryjliu0
reviewedPosts.text:
A lot of real-world documents embed extremely dense charts that require humans to not only "perceive" the chart values, but also reason over them and reconcile with other complex elements (e.g. tables) to solve a knowledge task.

We've encoded this complex chart+document reasoning within our ExtractBench Pro benchmark, released yesterday. Even the best frontier models struggle at solving complex extraction tasks perfectly over these documents.

For more details on ExtractBench Pro, check out the blog: https://t.co/bwxs86iS1d

If you have complex extraction needs at scale, check out LlamaParse: https://t.co/XYZmx5TFz8
reviewedPosts.evidence: 发布ExtractBenchPro，以整篇提取全对率评估

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
最近试了下 AIPOCH Open-Science，一个面向 AI 科研的开源工作台。

简单说，就是让 Agent 参与真实科研流程：读数据、跑 Python/R、分析结果，同时把代码、文件和研究过程都保留下来。

我接上 Claude Fable 5.1，拿它复现了一个 AI 圈挺有名的研究：Epoch AI 对 Chinchilla scaling law 的复现。

用的是 Epoch 从论文配图里提取的 245 个公开数据点，按原论文的方法重新拟合，再和两篇论文的结果对比。

Agent 会自己查原论文、写代码拟合、算置信区间、生成图表和报告。拟合出的参数和 Epoch 论文基本一致，中途它还自己发现 scipy 默认的收敛容差会让置信区间偏窄，换了严格容差重跑。

但我更感兴趣的是它的 「.science」。

研究做完后，可以把会话、文件、Notebook 运行记录和验证信息一起打包。

官网放了不少 「.science」 的例子，大家可以参考 ↓

https://t.co/aCMHW6BABy

我实际导出再导入了一遍，比较直观的感受是：别人拿到的不只是最后几张图，还能顺着记录往回看，这个结果到底是怎么跑出来的。想接着做也能直接建副本，我就在副本里换成 MSE 又跑了一轮。

Epoch 当初要从论文配图里一个个抠数据点，缺的就是这样一份过程记录。

这其实挺接近我理解的「Vibe Research」。

让有研究想法的人更容易把想法真正跑起来，同时研究过程也更容易被检查、分享和复现。

如果这套方式继续成熟，科研的门槛确实还会再往下降一些。

Science, open to all.

AIPOCH Open-Science ↓

https://t.co/vkhls0KT4V

reviewedPosts.author: DrJimFan
reviewedPosts.text:
We are open-sourcing V1.0 of our agentic robotics framework, ASPIRE, with full real robot skill discovery and self improvement capabilities! On the day Astra arrived, our lab switched the backend model and saturated all the benchmarks to ~99% over night.

And the frontier is already on the move:
- Opus 5.5 slightly edges out Astra on our robot simulation bench.
- Sonnet 5.5 hits the Pareto frontier of cost vs. robot capability, $12/task. 

We first introduced ASPIRE and /robot skill library in June, way before the big models could reliably do robotics. A rising frontier tide lifts all boats, but Astra was a 0->1 tsunami on many tasks.

Now you can also feel the Physical Bitter Lesson at home like we did on that fateful day ;)
